adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 33.7. The target week has no event, but a price increase to $5.03 (+6.3% vs regular $4.73). Recent weeks at $5.03 show median sales of 42.5 (2026-03-30: 42 units, 2026-04-06: 23 units). The 2026-03-30 week was Easter, a holiday, so not comparable. The 2026-04-06 week (post-Easter, no promotion) sold 23 units, below baseline. No past week at $5.03 with no holiday shows uplift. Price increases typically depress demand. The noise-adjusted effect of price hikes is not well-established, and evidence is thin. Confidence is low. No promotion or event, so no uplift. The median is adjusted down slightly due to price increase, but not enough to justify a strong signal.

  events: none
  shelf price: 5.03 (+6.3% vs regular price 4.73)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 33.7 | 5%-95%: 15.5 - 47.0 | 10%-90%: 20.3 - 46.1

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-44% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
